ranges.en: Ahiyah also erred and sealed the matter, since Jehu was a great righteous man.
Second Kings cites God's promise to Jehu for doing right, and that Jehu did not turn from Jeroboam's sins.
Asks what caused Jehu to be given such a promise despite his deeds.
Abaye: the covenant with Jehu was made only with the lips, not in the heart.
Second Kings: Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him a lot.
Rava says Ahiyah's seal means he saw the matter and erred.
Hosea 5:2 cited: they deepened the slaughter at Shittim, and I rebuke them all.
Rabbi Yohanan quotes God saying they deepened the matter, and that whoever does not go up to the festival violates a positive commandment.
First Kings 11:29 cited on the one who goes up to the festival being struck by the sword.
Jeroboam leaves Jerusalem and meets Ahiyah the prophet on the road, hidden in a new Shiloh.
A Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: that moment is appointed for punishment.
Jeremiah 51:18 cited: in the time of their punishment they shall perish.
Another Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: a time is appointed for punishment.
Isaiah 49:8 cited: in a time of favor I have answered you.
Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: a time is appointed for good.
Exodus 32:34 cited: in the day I punish, I will punish their sin.
Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: that moment is appointed for punishment.
Genesis 38:1 cited: at that time Judah went down from his brothers.
Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: a time is appointed for punishment.
First Kings 12:1 cited: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to crown him.
Tanna from Rabbi Yosei: Shechem is a place appointed for punishment.
Examples from Shechem: Shimon and Levi attacked after Dinah was violated, and his brothers sold Joseph there.
The kingdom of David's house was divided at that place.
First Kings 11:29 cited on the division of the kingdom.
Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa says Jeroboam left Jerusalem through the gate of the city.
First Kings 11:29 cited again.
Ahiyah met Jeroboam on the road, and both were alone in the field.
Asks what the new Shiloh in the verse refers to.
Rav Nachman: just as the new Shiloh had no defect, Jeroboam's teaching had no defect.
Another explanation: the new Shiloh is one that brought new matters never heard before.
Asks what the phrase both alone in the field means.
Rav Yehuda says in Rav's name that all Sages are like the grasses of the field before them.
Some say all the reasons of the Torah are revealed to them, like a field.
Micah 1:14 cited: you shall give parting gifts to the kings of Israel, as Achzib deceives.
Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa says a heavenly voice told them who killed the Philistine should be given Gath as a parting gift.
Rav Hinena bar Pappa: whoever benefits from this world without blessing is as if robbing God and the Congregation of Israel.
Proverbs 28:24 and Deuteronomy 32:6 and Proverbs 1:8 cited, identifying the Holy One as father and Congregation of Israel as mother.
Asks what it means to be a companion of a corrupt man.
It refers to Jeroboam son of Nevat, who corrupted Israel against their Father in heaven.
Second Kings 17:21 cited: Jeroboam drove Israel from following God and led them into a great sin.
Rabbi Hanin says they are like two sticks that strike each other, with the verse about gold.
Deuteronomy 1:1 cited: between Paran and Tophel and Laban.
The Sages of Rabbi Yannai's school say Moses told God that the silver and gold he gave Israel led them to make idols, until they said enough.
That gold led them to make golden gods.
A proverb: a lion roars from a basket of straw, but not from a basket of meat.
Rabbi Oshaya: until Jeroboam Israel nursed from one calf, and from then on, from two and three calves.
Rabbi Yitzhak: every punishment that comes to the world has at least one twenty-fourth of the weight of the first calf.
Exodus 32:34 cited: in the day I punish, I will punish their sin.
Rabbi Hanina says that after twenty-four generations this verse was fulfilled.
Ezekiel 9:1 cited: a loud voice called for the city's punishers, each with his weapon in hand.
First Kings 13:33 cited: after this matter Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way.
Asks what the word after refers to.
Rabbi Abba: God seized Jeroboam by his garment and said, return, and you and I and the son of Yishai will walk in Eden.
Jeroboam replies that if Jesse's son is first, he does not want to be in the same place.
Rabbi Avahu used to expound three kings, and when he was weak he accepted that he should not expound, since once...

ranges.en: A rabbi is rebuked for expounding on the three kings after agreeing not to do so.
Asks whether the others retracted their expounding of the three kings.
Rav Ashi says he himself retracted and set aside the three kings.
Next day, Manasseh appears to the teacher in a dream.
Manasseh asks from where the teacher intends to permit the blessing of hamotzi.
The teacher says he does not know.
Manasseh replies that he has not learned it, though he has taught others to derive it.
The teacher asks Manasseh to teach him, promising to expound it in his name.
Manasseh asks from where one derives the rule about cooking.
Manasseh asks why, having learned so much, the teacher still serves idols.
Manasseh says that had he been there, he would have grabbed the hem of the cloak and run after him.
The next day he tells the Sages to begin with the great ones: Ahab, brother to Heaven and father to idolatry.
Proverbs 17:17 and Psalms 103:13 cited to explain the brother and father images.
First Kings 16:31 cited: it was a light matter for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam.
Rabbi Yohanan says Ahab's light sins equal Jeroboam's grave ones.
Asks why Scripture attributes the sin to Jeroboam.
Because Jeroboam was the first to lead Israel into corruption.
Hosea 12:12 cited about altars like heaps on the furrows of the field.
Rabbi Yohanan says every furrow in the Land of Israel had an idol that Ahab set up for worship.
Asks how we know Ahab has no share in the World-to-Come.
First Kings 21:21 cited: Ahab's sons will be cut off, one who is restrained in this world is forsaken in the next.
Rabbi Yohanan asks why Omri merited kingship.
Because he added one city in the Land of Israel, as the verse says.
First Kings 16:24 cited on Omri buying the hill of Samaria and naming the city after Shemer.
Rabbi Yohanan asks why Ahab merited kingship for twenty-two years.
Because he honored the Torah, which was given in twenty-two letters.
First Kings 20:2 cited: Ahab received messengers from Ben-Hadad.
Ben-Hadad's demand for Ahab's wealth and family and the reply that the first demand will be met, but not this one.
Asks what the desire of your eyes means, and whether it is not a Torah scroll.
Perhaps it means idolatry? No, that is not the meaning.
First Kings 20:8 cited: the elders and people tell him not to agree and not to listen.
Asks whether perhaps those were foolish elders, since it is not written that way.
Second Samuel 17:4 cited: the advice was right in Absalom's eyes and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
Rav Yosef says the elders of foolishness are not described with all the people, but here it is written, and righteous ones must have been among them.
First Kings 19:18 cited: seven thousand in Israel who did not kneel to Baal and did not kiss him.
Rav Nachman says Ahab was balanced between good and bad.
First Kings 22:20 cited: God asks who will entice Ahab, and Ahab falls at Ramoth-Gilead.
Rav Yosef objects: who wrote about him that there was none like Ahab in his wickedness?
First Kings 21:25 cited: none was like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil, and Jezebel incited him.
Rather, Ahab was generous with his wealth, and Torah scholars atoned for him with half of his property.
First Kings 22:21 cited.
The quote of the spirit that goes out and becomes a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths.
Asks what spirit means here.
Rabbi Yohanan says it is the spirit of Naboth the Jezreelite.
Asks what go out means.
Ravina says it means go out from my presence.
Psalms 101:7 cited: one who speaks lies shall not be established before my eyes.
Rav Pappa says this is what people say: one who spoils his nest ruins his house.
First Kings 16:33 cited.
Ahab made the Asherah and added to provoke God more than all previous kings of Israel.
Rabbi Yohanan says Ahab wrote on Samaria's doors denying the God of Israel, so he has no share in Him.
Second Chronicles 22:9 cited: they sought Ahaziah, who was hiding in Samaria.
Rabbi Levi says Manasseh used to erase divine names and write idols in their place.
Another explanation: Manasseh made Israel deny their Father in heaven.
Asks how we know Manasseh does not enter the World-to-Come, as it is written.
Second Chronicles 33:1 and Second Kings 21:3 cited: Manasseh did evil as Ahab had done.
Just as Ahab has no share in the World-to-Come, so Manasseh has none.
Rabbi Yehuda says Manasseh does have a share in the World-to-Come.
Second Chronicles 33:13 cited: Manasseh prayed to God, who was entreated by him.
Rabbi Yohanan says both sides interpret the same verse.
Jeremiah 15:4 cited: I will make them a horror among all kingdoms because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah.
One side holds the punishment was because of Manasseh, who repented, while the other side holds it was due to his sins.

ranges.en: The punishment came because of Manasseh, who did not repent.
Rabbi Yohanan says whoever claims Manasseh has no share in the World-to-Come weakens penitents' hands.
A Tanna taught before Rabbi Yohanan that Manasseh repented, over thirty-three years.
Second Kings 21:1 cited on Manasseh's reign and Ahab's, with the year counts compared.
Rabbi Yohanan says in the name of Rashbi.
Asks what is meant by the verse written in that place.
Second Chronicles 33:13 cited: God heard Manasseh's prayer and restored him.
Asks why the text needed to say he was entreated, as if it were a breach.
God made a breach in heaven to receive Manasseh in repentance, balancing the attribute of justice.
Rabbi Yohanan again says in the name of Rashbi.
Asks what is written in the verses about kings.
Jeremiah 26:1 and 28:1 cited: the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign and of Zedekiah's reign.
Asks whether there were no kings until then.
God wanted to return the world to chaos because of Jehoiakim, but calmed when He looked at Zedekiah's generation.
Second Kings 24:9 cited: he did evil, and could have prevented it but did not.
Rabbi Yohanan, in the name of Rashbi, adds a further teaching.
Asks what is written in Proverbs.
Proverbs 29:9 cited: a wise man contends with a foolish man, who rages and laughs with no rest.
God says he was angry with Ahaz and gave him into the hand of the kings of Damascus, who beat him and sacrificed to their gods.
Second Chronicles 28:23 cited: Ahaz sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, saying they help the kings of Aram.
Second Chronicles 25:14 cited: Amaziah brought back the gods of the Edomites and bowed to them.
Rav Pappa says this is what people say: weep for one who does not know, and woe to one who cannot tell good from bad.
Jeremiah 39:3 cited: the officers of the king of Babylon sat in the middle gate.
Rabbi Yohanan, in the name of Rashbi, says it is a place where laws are cut.
Rav Pappa says it is like the saying: where a master's weapon hangs, the shepherd hangs his bag, with a mnemonic on fields and houses.
Rav Hisda says Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba teaches this.
Asks what is written in Proverbs 24:30.
Proverbs 24:30 cited: I passed by the field of the lazy man and the vineyard of the man lacking sense.
The verse is read allegorically: the field is Ahaz, the vineyard is Manasseh, and the thorns and walls are Amon, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah, when the Temple was destroyed.
Rav Hisda says Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba teaches that four groups do not receive the Divine Presence.
The four groups are scoffers, deceivers, flatterers, and slanderers.
Hosea 7:5 cited about scoffers.
Psalms 101:7 cited about those who speak lies.
Job 13:16 cited about the flatterer who comes before God.
Psalms 5:5 cited about the slanderer, that God does not desire wickedness and no evil dwells with Him.
Rav Hisda says Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba teaches a further point.
Asks what is written in Psalms 91.
Psalms 91:10 cited: no evil will befall you, and no plague will come near your tent.
The verse is read as protection from the evil inclination, from wrongful thoughts, and from a son or student who spoils a dish publicly.
Psalms 91:11 cited: God commands His angels to guard you in all your ways.
Up to here the blessing is from the father, and from here on the blessing is from the mother, and then from heaven.

ranges.en: Psalm verse promising deliverance, protection and honor to one who loves God
Resh Lakish is introduced as the source of the following teaching
Asks what the Job verse about withholding light from the wicked means
Asks why the letter ayin in the word for wicked is written raised above the line
Explains that one made poor below becomes poor above, so the ayin is suspended
Objects that if so, the letter should simply not have been written at all
Two answers: the letter was kept to honor David, and to honor Nehemiah ben Hachaliah
A baraita says Manasseh, Ahab and Jeroboam studied many aspects of Torat Kohanim
Rabbi Meir rules that Absalom has no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Samuel verse on Absalom's death, read as two kinds of death
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, citing Rabbi Meir, denies the evil kings of Israel a share in the World-to-Come and judgment
Cites the Kings verse on Manasseh shedding much innocent blood and leading Judah astray
Babylonian tradition reads that blood as Manasseh killing Isaiah
Western tradition says Manasseh made a huge idol that killed a thousand people carrying it daily
Asks whose opinion stands behind the teaching that one righteous soul outweighs the whole world
Answers that it follows the view that Manasseh killed Isaiah
Two Chronicles verses use the singular and plural words for idol about Manasseh
Rabbi Yochanan reconciles them: first one face, later four, so the Divine Presence would see and be angered
Ahaz placed the idol in the upper chamber
Cites the Kings verse about the altars on the roof of Ahaz's upper chamber
Manasseh placed the idol inside the Temple sanctuary
Cites the Kings verse where God says His name will dwell in this house
Amon brought the idol into the Holy of Holies
Cites Isaiah's verse about a bed too short and a covering too narrow
Asks what it means that the bed is too short
Explains the bed is too short for two rivals, since God's service and idolatry cannot share it
Asks what it means that the covering is too narrow
Rabbi Yonatan wept whenever he reached this verse, showing grief over idolatry in the Temple
Cites a Psalm about God gathering the sea, arguing a graven image cannot rival Him
Ahaz nullified the Temple service and sealed the Torah from study
Cites Isaiah's verse about binding the testimony and sealing the Torah among disciples
Manasseh erased the divine names from sacred books and removed the remembrances
Manasseh destroyed the altar, and Amon burned the Torah and offered a creeping animal on the altar
Ahaz permitted forbidden sexual relations and declared such marriages allowed
Manasseh relied on that ruling to lie with his sister, and Amon with his mother
Cites a Chronicles verse saying Amon's guilt was great, supporting the account of his sins
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree: one says Amon burned the Torah, the other that he lay with his mother
His mother asks whether he gets any pleasure from the place he came out of
He replies that he acts only to provoke his Creator, not for his own pleasure
Jehoiakim says earlier kings did not know how to defy God and asks why they need His light
Jehoiakim proposes using shining gold so that God's light could be taken away
Objectors reply that the silver and gold are God's own
Cites the Haggai verse saying the silver and gold are God's
Jehoiakim replies that God has already given them to us
Cites the Psalm saying the heavens belong to God and the earth was given to people
Rava asks why Jehoiakim is not counted among kings denied a share in the World-to-Come
Gives the reason one might think he is excluded: a verse is written about him
Cites the Chronicles verse about Jehoiakim's abominations and what was found on him
Asks what the phrase about what was found on him means
Two views: he engraved an idol's name on a private part of his body, or God's name in contempt
Rabba bar Mari replies that he heard the reason for excluding a commoner, though not for the kings
Asks why Micah is not counted among those denied a share in the World-to-Come
Micah offered his bread to passersby, which is the reason for his favor
Cites the Zechariah verse about all who pass by the Levites
Cites a verse about passing through the sea with affliction and striking the waves
Rabbi Yochanan explains that this affliction refers to Micah's idol
A baraita says the smoke of Shiloh's altar mixed with the smoke of Micah's idol across three mil
The ministering angels wanted to push Micah away, but God said to leave him for his hospitality
The Gibeah punishment is tied to Micah's idol, and God rebukes Israel for protesting human honor instead of His
Rabbi Yochanan, citing Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma, says great eating distanced two clans from Israel
Cites the Deuteronomy verse barring Ammonites and Moabites for not meeting Israel with bread and water
Rabbi Yochanan's own view: food distances the near, draws the distant, and makes unwitting sin count as willful
The Gemara starts to elaborate how food distances the near, which it goes on to derive

ranges.en: Continues the derivation that food distances the near, citing Ammon and Moab, and draws the distant, citing Yitro
Rabbi Yochanan says the reward for Yitro was given in return for his hospitality
Cites the Exodus verse where Yitro tells his daughters to call Moses to eat bread
Yitro's descendants merited sitting in the Chamber of Hewn Stone
Cites the Chronicles verse about the Kenite scribes descended from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab
Cites the Judges verse about the Kenites, Moses' in-laws, who went up with Judah and settled among the people
Food averts eyes from the wicked, as with Micah, and draws the Divine Presence onto Baal's prophets
The same applies to the neighbor of the prophet Iddo
Cites the Kings verse about the prophet who was deceived while sitting at the table
An unwitting sin that involved food is counted as a deliberate one
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says two loaves would have saved Nob, Doeg and Saul's sons from death
Asks why Ahaz was not counted among the kings who have no share in the World-to-Come
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says Ahaz lies between two righteous kings, Yotam and Hezekiah
Rav Yosef says Ahaz was too ashamed before Isaiah to be counted
Cites Isaiah's verse in which God tells him to go out to Ahaz at the fuller's field
Asks what the word fuller refers to in that verse
Two explanations: one says the fuller pressed him face down and passed, the other that the harvest cut off his head
Asks why Amon was not counted among those with no share in the World-to-Come
Because of the honor of Josiah, his son
Asks why Manasseh was likewise not counted
Because of the honor of Hezekiah, Manasseh's father
A principle: a son does not mention the father and a father does not mention the son
Cites the Deuteronomy verse that no one can save from God, and Abraham could not save Ishmael or Isaac save Esau
Now that you have come to this, Ahaz too was not counted, out of the honor of Hezekiah
Asks why Jehoiakim was not counted among those with no share in the World-to-Come
Because of Rabbi Chiya bar Avuya, who gives a reason tied to a skull inscription
Rabbi Chiya bar Avuya says it is written on the skull of Jehoiakim
Rabbi Pereida's grandfather found a skull thrown at the Jerusalem gates bearing the inscription this and another
The inscription says it was buried yet not buried, and the skull is identified as Jehoiakim's
Cites the Jeremiah verse that Jehoiakim shall be buried like a donkey, dragged and cast out
Hezekiah's people said he was a king, not fit to be treated shamefully, so they wrapped the skull in silk and placed it in a box
His wife thought it was the first woman, since they did not forget her, and so the inscription says this and another
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says that for the sake of Hezekiah's words God granted him a sign
Cites the Kings verse where Hezekiah says he did what is good in God's eyes
Asks what sign was given for this
Cites the Kings verse about the sign of the shadow and about foreigners eating at his table
Because foreigners ate at Hezekiah's table, the exile came upon his descendants
This supports Hezekiah's principle that whoever brings idolaters into his home causes exile for his children
Cites Kings and Isaiah on Hezekiah's descendants becoming eunuchs, and Hezekiah showing Babylon's envoys his treasure house
Rav asks what is meant by house of treasure
Rav says it means his wife, who made the envoys drink
Shmuel says it means his storehouse of treasures, which he showed them
Rabbi Yochanan says it means the members of his body, which he showed them
Cites the Lamentations verse about how the city sits alone
Rava relays Rabbi Yochanan asking why Israel was punished with the word eikhah
Because they transgressed the thirty-six karitot in the Torah
Rabbi Yochanan asks why Israel was punished with the alef-bet letters
Because they transgressed the Torah that was given in the alef-bet letters
Notes the alef-bet structure and cites the verse that she sits alone
Rabbi Yochanan says God declared that He said Israel would dwell securely
Cites the Deuteronomy verse that Israel dwells in safety, and the verse that now their dwelling will be alone
Cites the Lamentations verse about the great city full of people
Rabbi Yochanan explains they married the young to the old and the old to the young so they would have many children
Cites the Lamentations verse that she is like a widow
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, explains it as a wife whose husband went overseas and intends to return
Cites the Lamentations verse that she is great among nations and a princess among provinces
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says wherever they go they become princes to their masters
A baraita tells of two people taken captive on Mount Carmel, with a pursuer following after them
