ranges.en: Introduces the story of a blind camel carrying wine and oil, led by one Jew and one gentile
The gentile challenges them, asking how they know, calling the Jews a stiff-necked people
The Jews explain that the camel ate only from the side it could see, showing it was blind in one eye
They explain the load: wine dripped and sank while oil dripped and floated, showing which skin leaked
They identify the two leaders, one gentile and one Jew, as the source of the knowledge
They explain the gentile turned toward the road while the Jew turned aside, showing their differing paths
The gentile follows them, finds it as they said, and kisses their heads before bringing them home
The host makes a feast and dances, blessing God who chose Abraham's seed, and the guests return home in peace
Cites the Lamentations verse about weeping bitterly at night
Asks why there are these two separate cries of weeping
Rabbi Yochanan says one cry is for the first Temple and one for the second, both at night, for night reasons
Cites the Numbers verse about the congregation weeping that night
Rabba and Rabbi Yochanan say that night was the ninth of Av
God tells Israel they wept a weeping for nothing and will set this weeping for the generations
Other explanations: the night weeper's voice is heard, and the stars and constellations weep with him
Another explanation: whoever hears the nightly weeping's voice weeps in response to it
A woman weeps over her son at night, and Rabban Gamliel weeps in response until his eyelashes fall out
Cites the Lamentations verse about her tears on her cheek
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, explains she is like a woman weeping for the husband of her youth
Cites the Joel verse about a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth
Cites the Lamentations verse that her adversaries became the head
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says whoever distresses Israel becomes the head
Cites the Isaiah verse about the lands of Zebulun, Naphtali and the region beyond the Jordan
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says whoever oppresses Israel is not weary
Cites the Lamentations verse that it is nothing to you, all who pass by the way
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says this verse allows one to complain against the Torah
Rav Amram, citing Rav, says they made us like those who transgressed the law
Contrasts Sodom and Jerusalem by citing the Genesis verse about Sodom and the Lamentations verses about Jerusalem
Asks whether there is partiality in this matter
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says Jerusalem had a greater measure of sin than Sodom
Cites the Ezekiel verse on Sodom's sin of pride and neglect of the poor
Cites Lamentations verses on Jerusalem's women eating their children and the enemies' mockery
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, asks why the letter pe precedes the letter ayin in the acrostic
Because the spies spoke with their mouths what their eyes had not seen
Cites the Psalm about those who eat my people as bread and do not call upon God
Rava, citing Rabbi Yochanan, says whoever eats Israel's bread tastes it, and whoever does not is not counted as calling God
Rav says the ones who eat the people are the judges
Shmuel says they are the teachers of children
Asks who appointed these people
Rav Ashi says the men of the Great Assembly appointed them
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says they sought to appoint one more, and an image of his father appeared
The image of the father spread itself before them, and they paid it no attention
Fire came from heaven and licked their benches, and they still paid it no attention
A heavenly voice came out and spoke to them
Cites the Proverbs verse about a man diligent in his work standing before kings
The Gemara explains: one who built his house before mine, indeed I built mine in seven years and his in thirteen
Repeats the Proverbs verse about standing before kings
The heavenly voice did not heed him and came out and spoke
Cites the Job verse saying God will repay as you choose, not as I do
Interpreters of records all say that everyone comes to the World-to-Come
Cites the Psalm listing Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim and Judah as God's possessions
Each name in the Psalm is read as a person: Ahab, Manasseh literally, Jeroboam, and Ahitophel

105a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Explains the Psalm's names: Moab is the pot of washing, meaning Gehazi, and Doeg the Edomite is meant by the shoe
The ministering angels ask God what He will do if David comes, since David killed Goliath and dispossessed Gath
God replies that it is up to Him to make the two of them friends with each other
Cites the Jeremiah verse asking why this people turned away in perpetual backsliding
Rav explains that nitzchat means the congregation of Israel answered the prophet with repentance
The prophet tells Israel to return in repentance, asking where their ancestors who sinned are
Israel objects: where are your prophets who did not sin?
Cites the Zechariah verse asking where your fathers are, and whether the prophets live forever
The prophet replies that the fathers did return and acknowledge their fault
Cites the Zechariah verse that God's words and statutes overtook the fathers
Shmuel says ten people came and sat before him, and he told them to return in repentance
They ask whether a slave sold by his master or a wife divorced by her husband can return, and whether there is any reply
God tells the prophet to say to them: Show me the bill of divorce of your mother that I sent away
Cites the Isaiah verse that you were sold for your sins, and your mother was sent away for your transgressions
This is what Resh Lakish said, and the Gemara asks what the verse means
Asks the meaning of what is written here
Cites the Jeremiah verse in which God calls Nebuchadnezzar My servant, in addition to David
Explains that God, knowing Israel would say this, called His servant first, so the claim would not be made
A servant who acquires property, to whom does the property belong, to his master
Cites the Ezekiel verse that what enters your mind shall not happen, and that God will rule over you with a strong hand
Rav Nachman explains that whenever the Merciful One is angry with us, He does so in order to redeem us
Cites the Isaiah verse that his God instructs him in the right judgment
Rabba bar bar Hana says a prophet told Israel to return in repentance
They reply that they cannot, because the evil inclination controls them
The prophet replies: discipline your inclinations
They retort: may his God instruct him, if the prophet can instruct them
Four commoners are named: Balaam, Doeg, Ahitophel and Gehazi
Explains that this Balaam is a different person from the Balaam who swallowed the people, and identifies him with Laban the Aramean
Asks what his name was, and whether it was Laban the Aramean
Cites the Numbers verse that Balaam was the son of Beor
Cites the Numbers verse that Balaam was the son of Beor, as the verse says in another place
Rabbi Yochanan explains that his father and son refer to Balaam's prophecy
Balaam is the one who has no share in the World-to-Come, and the Mishnah's ruling is taught accordingly
Asks whose opinion this Mishnah follows
It is Rabbi Yehoshua's view, as taught in a baraita
Cites the Psalm verse that the wicked shall return to the grave, along with all nations that forget God
Rabbi Eliezer explains the verse: the wicked are Israel's sinners, and the nations who forgot God are idolaters
Rabbi Yehoshua objects: does the verse say all the nations? It says only that the wicked shall return to the grave
Asks who are the nations that forgot God
All nations who forgot God, and that wicked man himself gave the sign by his own words
Cites Balaam's words in Numbers: let me die the death of the righteous, and let my end be like theirs
Cites the Numbers verse that the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went out
A tanna taught that Midian and Moab never had peace with one another
A parable of two dogs in a flock that bark at each other until a wolf attacks one, and both are killed
Rav Pappa says this is the proverb people use, that a frog and a cat held a wedding, a big feast
Cites the Numbers verse that the officers of Moab sat with Balaam
The officers of Midian ask where they should go once Balaam told them to stay the night
Cites Balaam's words in Numbers: stay here tonight, and I will bring you word
They ask whether there is any father who hates his son
Rav Nachman says chutzpah helps even against heaven, at least at the beginning
Cites the verse that you shall not go with them
Ultimately it is written: arise, go with them
Rav Sheshet says insolence is characteristic of kingship, which cannot survive without a crown
Cites the Samuel verse about David, who is tender and anointed king, and the men of Zeruiah who are harder than he
Rabbi Yochanan says Balaam was lame in one leg, as the verse states
Cites the Numbers verse that Balaam went limping, and the Genesis verse about a viper biting a horse's heels
Balaam was blind in one eye, as stated in the verse
Cites the Numbers verse about the man with a closed eye, a diviner in his truth
Compares the Numbers verse about falling with open eyes to the Esther verse about Haman falling on the couch
Mar Zutra says Balaam was a diviner in his truth
Mar bar Ravina says Balaam had relations with his donkey
Explains that the one who says diviner in truth holds as stated before
Cites the Numbers verse about bowing down and lying down, and the Judges verse about bowing between her feet

105b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Opens the Balaam verse about falling down and lying down, citing Numbers 24:16
If he knew his beast's knowledge, how could he not know the knowledge of the Most High? Asks what knowledge of the beast means
Explains the story: the donkey tells Balaam she carried him all his life and now is doing something new at night
Cites the Numbers verse where the donkey asks, am I not your donkey on which you have ridden
Cites the Kings verse where Abishag was a companion to David
Asks what is meant by Balaam knowing the knowledge of the Most High
Balaam knew how to time the moment when God was angry with the beast
This is what the prophet said to Israel
Cites the Micah verse asking the people to remember what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam answered
Asks what the phrase so that you may know the righteous acts of the Lord means
God tells Israel that during Balaam's days He did not get angry, so no enemy of Israel remained as a survivor
This is what Balaam said to Balak
Cites the Numbers verse: how shall I curse whom God has not cursed, and God is not angry with them
God is angry every day, but His anger lasts only a moment
Cites the Psalm verse that His anger is for a moment, and His favor is for life
Alternatively, cites the Isaiah verse telling My people to enter their chambers and hide until the anger passes
Continues the Isaiah verse about hiding for a little while until the wrath passes
Describes the hours when God's anger is strong, and the rooster Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi used to torment
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi tied the rooster's leg and set it down, and when the hour came he fell asleep
He said: learn from this that it is not the way of the world to punish the righteous
Cites the Proverbs verse that punishing the righteous is not good, even in the matter of a bird
He should not have said such a thing
A tanna taught in the name of Rabbi Meir that when the sun rises and kings bow to it, God becomes angry at once
Cites the Numbers verse that Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey
A tanna taught in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar that love nullifies the power of greatness, greater than Abraham's
Cites the Genesis verse about Abraham rising early and the Numbers verse about Balaam rising early to saddle his donkey
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says a person should always engage in Torah and mitzvot, even not for their own sake
Balak's forty-two offerings earned the birth of Ruth from him
Rabbi Yossi bar Hunah says Ruth was the daughter of Eglon, son of Balak king of Moab
Rava objects to Rabba bar Mari: the verse says God will make Solomon's name better than yours, which seems improper to say to a king
Rabba bar Mari answers that she spoke in a veiled way, so that you would not say such a thing
Cites the Judges verse blessing Jael, wife of Chever the Kenite, among women
Asks who the women mentioned are
Sarah, Rivka, Rachel and Leah; it is not the way of the world to say so, but it is veiled speech, and so here too
This disagrees with Rav Yosei bar Chuni, who says every person is jealous except of his son and disciple
Alternatively, cites the Kings verse asking for a double portion of Elijah's spirit
Cites the Numbers verse where Moses laid his hands on Joshua and charged him
Cites the Numbers verse that God put a word in Balaam's mouth
Rabbi Eliezer says an angel put the word in his mouth, while Rabbi Yonatan says a hook did
Rabbi Yochanan explains that Balaam wanted to say there would be no synagogues or study halls among them
Cites the Numbers verse: how goodly are your tents, O Jacob
The Gemara lists the curses Balaam intended, such as the Shekhina not resting on them, and their rulers and kingdoms failing
Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says all the curses turned into blessings except for synagogues and study halls
Cites the Deuteronomy verse that God turned the curse into a blessing because He loved you
Shmuel bar Nachmani, citing Rabbi Yonatan, comments on the curse in Proverbs
Asks what the verse in Proverbs means
Cites the Proverbs verse that the wounds of a friend are faithful and the kisses of an enemy are deceitful
The curse Ahiyah the Shilonite pronounced on Israel was stronger than the blessing Balaam the wicked gave them
Cites the Kings verse that God will strike Israel as the reed is shaken in water, and asks what kind of reed stands in water

106a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Explains the reed: even when every wind blows on it, it does not move from its place, once the winds calm it stands again
Balaam the wicked blessed them with a cedar, which does not stand in a place of water
The cedar has shallow roots, a south wind uproots it, while the reed merits a quill to write Torah, Prophets and Writings
Cites the Numbers verse where Balaam saw the Kenite and spoke to Yitro's people, asking who placed them near the eternal ones
Rabbi Chiya bar Abba, citing Rabbi Simai, says three were in that counsel: Balaam was killed, Job was silent and punished, Yitro fled and was rewarded
Cites the Chronicles verse about the families of scribes who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone
Cites the Judges verse about the Kenites, Moses' in-laws, who went up from the city of palm trees
Cites the Numbers verse where Balaam saw the Kenite, and lifted up his parable, saying woe who shall live
Resh Lakish explains: woe to one who makes himself live by the name of God
Rabbi Yochanan says woe to the nation found when God performs redemption for His children
Who casts his covering between a lion and a lioness when they come together, meaning Israel and the nations at their meeting
Cites the Numbers verse about ships from Kittim
Rav says Lebun is Aspir
Cites the Numbers verse about Ashur and Eber, which afflicted Ashur
From here on, killers will be killed and enslavers will be enslaved
Cites the Numbers verse where Balaam says he goes to his people and will advise what this people will do
Asks why the verse says to this people rather than another phrasing
Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says Balaam was like a person who curses himself and places his curse on others
Balaam tells them their God hates lewdness, and that they should come, so he would advise them
Balaam's scheme: set up booths, seat old women outside and young women inside, and sell them linen items
While Israel eats, drinks and goes out to stroll in the marketplace, the old woman says to him
The old woman asks whether he wants linen items
The old woman offers to sell at equal price, and the young one at less than twice or three times
Afterward she tells him: you are now like a member of the household, so take it for yourself
A flask of Ammonite wine was placed beside her, not yet forbidden like the wine of gentiles
She asks whether he wants to drink a cup of wine, and once he drank, he became inflamed with desire
She tells him to worship this idol
He objects: am I not a Jew?
She replies that they only ask him for lewdness, and that she will not leave him unless he denies Moses his teacher's Torah
Cites the Hosea verse about Baal-Peor and the Numbers verse that Israel dwelt in Shittim
Rabbi Eliezer says Shittim is the name of a place; Rabbi Yehoshua says they engaged in foolish talk that led them to sacrifice to idols
Rabbi Elazar says the naked women met them; Rabbi Yehoshua says they all became men with seminal emissions
Asks the meaning of the word Rephidim
Rabbi Eliezer says Rephidim is the name of a place
Rabbi Yehoshua says they weakened themselves in regard to the words of the Torah
Cites the Jeremiah verse that the fathers did not turn to their children from weakness of hands
Rabbi Yochanan says wherever the word vayeshev appears it signifies distress
Cites the Numbers verse that Israel dwelt in Shittim and began to whore with the daughters of Moab
Cites the Genesis verse that Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojourning, and Joseph brought their evil report
Cites the Genesis verse that Israel dwelt in the land of Goshen, and the days of Israel drew near to die
Cites the Kings verse that Judah and Israel dwelt safely, each under his vine and fig tree
Cites the Kings verse about God raising up an adversary to Solomon, and the Numbers verse about slaying the kings of Midian
Balaam son of Beor was slain by the sword
Asks what Balaam was seeking there
Rabbi Yochanan says he went to take a reward of twenty-four thousand that he caused to fall among Israel
Mar Zutra, citing Rav, says this is the proverb: the camel went seeking horns and its ears were cut off
Cites the Joshua verse that Balaam son of Beor the diviner was killed by the children of Israel
Balaam was a diviner who was also a prophet, and Rabbi Yochanan explains he was first a prophet and then a diviner
Rav Pappa says this is the proverb: the one who once ruled over men became a carpenter

106b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Cites the Joshua verse that the children of Israel killed them by the sword along with their slain
Rav says Balaam underwent all four forms of capital punishment: stoning, burning, decapitation and strangulation
A heretic asks Rabbi Chanina how old Balaam was when he died
Rabbi Chanina says it is not written, but derived from the verse about men of blood and deceit not living out their days
Cites the Psalm verse about men of blood and deceit not living half their days, from which the age is derived
The heretic says Rabbi Chanina speaks well and asks to see Balaam's register
The register says Balaam was thirty-three years old when Pinchas killed him as a robber
Mar bar Ravina tells his son not to interpret all of these, only Balaam the wicked
Balaam the wicked is the exception, from whom much can be derived, since the Torah writes his name
Asks why the name Doeg is written with two different spellings
Rabbi Yochanan says God first sat and wondered whether Doeg would leave, and woe that he left, with a mnemonic of traits
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is meant by the verse
Cites the Psalm verse asking why the mighty man boasts of evil, and that God's kindness endures all day
God tells Doeg he is not mighty in Torah, so why does he boast of evil, while God's kindness is over him all day
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is meant by the verse about the wicked and God's statutes
Cites the Psalm verse: to the wicked God said, what right do you have to recount My statutes
God rebukes the wicked Doeg: when you reach the passages on murderers and slander, what do you expound about them
Cites the Psalm verse: you have put My covenant in your mouth
Rabbi Immi says Doeg's Torah was only on his lips and no further
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is meant by the verse about the righteous fearing and laughing at the wicked
Cites the Psalm verse that the righteous will see and fear, and laugh at him
At first they fear, and in the end they laugh
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is meant by the verse
Cites the Job verse about swallowing wealth and God casting it out of his belly
David asks God to let Doeg die, and God answers with the words about swallowing wealth and being cast out
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is meant by the verse that God will break you forever
Cites the Psalm verse that God will break you forever
God tells David to let Doeg come to the World-to-Come
David says that God will break him forever in response
Asks what is written in the verse about being plucked from the tent
Cites the Psalm verse that God will pluck him from the tent and uproot him from the land of the living
God says to let this teaching be learned in the house of study; David says it should be a building for the sages
Rabbi Yitzchak asks what is written in the Isaiah verse about the scribe and the weigher
Cites the Isaiah verse: where is the scribe, where is the one who weighs, where is the counter of towers
The verse refers to the scribe who counts all the letters of the Torah and the weigher who weighs light and heavy laws, and Doeg wrote three hundred laws in the flying tower
Four hundred questions were asked of Doeg and Ahitophel in the flying tower, and none was resolved
Rava says it is remarkable to raise questions on Rav Yehuda's two teachings, since all these are learned in tort law
We learn much about the stems of vegetables in Ukatzin
Rav Yehuda ruled on a woman pickling vegetables in a pot, and olives pickled in their brine are pure
Rav and Shmuel's teachings are seen here, while in Ukatzin we learn that thirteen sessions were held
Rav Yehuda took off his shoes and rain came, and we cry out, and no one pays attention
No one pays attention except God, who desires the heart
Cites the Samuel verse that God looks at the heart
Rav says Doeg and Ahitophel did not regard teaching from their roots
Mar Zutra objects: about whom is it written where is the scribe and where is the weigher, if you say they did not think teaching
Reply: they did regard the teaching, but it did not rise to them because it was not according to the halakhah
Cites the Psalm verse that the counsel of God is for those who fear Him
Rabbi Immi says Doeg did not die until he forgot his learning
Cites the Proverbs verse that he shall die for lack of instruction and be led astray by his great folly
Rav Ashi says Doeg became a leper
Cites the Psalm verse that You destroy everyone who goes astray from You
Cites the Leviticus verse about a house sold in perpetuity
The Aramaic translation renders it as completely, and we learn in the Mishnah that the difference between a sealed and an absolute ruling is a clause
A mnemonic for the list of the three who saw and the half who called
Rabbi Yochanan says three destroying angels met Doeg: one caused him to forget his learning, one burned his soul, and one scattered his dust in the houses of study
Rabbi Yochanan says Doeg and Ahitophel never saw each other: Doeg in Saul's days and Ahitophel in David's days
Rabbi Yochanan says Doeg and Ahitophel did not live out half their days, and a baraita teaches the same
A baraita says the men of blood and deceit did not live out half their days; Doeg lived thirty-four years and Ahitophel thirty-three
Rabbi Yochanan says David first called Ahitophel his master, then his colleague, then his student
David first called him master
Cites the Psalm verse: but you, a man my equal, my companion and my familiar
Later he called him a companion
Cites the Psalm verse about sharing sweet counsel together in the house of God
Finally he called him a student
Cites the Psalm verse: even the man of my peace in whom I trusted

107a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Opens with the Psalm verse about one who ate my bread lifting his heel against me
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says a person should never bring himself into a test, as David did and fell
David asks God why the Patriarchs are called God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, but not God of David
God replies that they were tested and you were not tested
David asks God to test him
Cites the Psalm verse: test me, O Lord, and try me
God says He will test David in a matter He did not tell them, and tells him directly that the test concerns a matter of nakedness
Cites the Samuel verse that at evening David rose from his bed and walked on the roof
Rav Yehuda says David turned his nightly bed into his daytime bed, and a small limb in a person satisfies him when hungry and hungers him when satisfied
Cites the Samuel verse about David rising at evening
Cites the Samuel verse about David walking on the roof of the king's house and seeing a woman bathing
Satan appeared as a bird, and the woman's head was under the cloth, and when the cloth was lifted David saw her immediately
Cites the Samuel verse about David sending to inquire about the woman, Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite
David sent and took her, and she purified herself, and the verse in Psalms about being tested at night is cited to support it
The scheme fell in the mouth of the one who hates me, but David did not say this, and Rava expounded it
Asks what is written in the Psalm superscription about fleeing like a bird
Cites the Psalm verse: in the Lord I have taken refuge, how can you say to my soul, flee like a bird to your mountain
David asks God to forgive him for that sin, so that they will not say your mountain was fled like a bird
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Psalm verse: against You alone I have sinned and done what is evil in Your eyes, so that You are justified
David says it is known to You that if I wanted to subdue my inclination I could, but I said they must not say the servant overcame his Master
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Psalm verse: for I am ready to limp, and my pain is always before me
Bathsheba was suitable for David from the six days of creation, but she came to him in pain
The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught the same: Bathsheba was suitable for David, daughter of Eliam, but she came to him in pain
Except that she had eaten an unripe fig
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Psalm verse: they gathered against me, and the wretched gathered, they tore me and I did not know, they did not cease
David tells God that if they tore his flesh, his blood would not flow, and that the court pauses its study while carrying out four forms of execution
They say to David: what is the death of one who lies with a married woman? I said: strangulation, and he has a share in the World-to-Come
But one who publicly shames his fellow has no share in the World-to-Come
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says even in David's sickness, his eighteen sins remained
Cites the Psalm verse: I am weary with my sighing, every night I drench my bed with tears
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says David sought to worship idols
Cites the Samuel verse that David came to the summit where one would bow down to God
The word summit can only mean idolatry
Cites the Daniel verse about the statue whose head was of fine gold, and the Samuel verse about Hushai
Cites the Samuel verse: Hushai the Archite met him with his garment torn and earth on his head
Hushai says: let them say a king like you worships idols
David replies: a king like me would be killed by his son; better he worship idols than profane God's name publicly
Asks what is the reason
You captured a beautiful woman
The Merciful One permitted a beautiful captive
You did not expound the supporting verse that follows it
Cites the Deuteronomy verse that whoever takes a beautiful woman may have a rebellious and defiant son
Rabbi Dostai of Biri asks why David is like a Cuthean merchant
David is like a Cuthean merchant who sells everything he has
David said to God: Master of the Universe
Cites the Psalm verse: who can discern his errors
David asks God to cleanse him of hidden faults, to keep his servant from presumptuous sins, and that the rabbis not rule over him
David says he will be cleansed of transgression, so that his fault will not be written
God says no: even the yod taken from Sarai stands and cries out
Explains that the yod was added to Joshua's name by Moses, so that the whole section is an argument a fortiori
Rav says David asked God to forgive him for the entire sin
It was already destined that Solomon, David's son, would say in his wisdom
Cites the Proverbs verse: can one walk on coals and not burn his feet, so too one who lies with his neighbor's wife
Whoever touches her will not go unpunished
Asks whether that man was so thrown out
He says: accept suffering upon yourself, and accept it on him
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says David became a leper for six months
David became a leper, the Shekhina departed from him, and the Sanhedrin withdrew from him
Cites the Psalm verse: purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean, wash me and I shall be whiter than snow
The Shekhina departed from him, as it is written
Cites the Psalm verse: restore to me the joy of Your salvation and sustain me with a willing spirit
The Sanhedrin withdrew from him, as it is written
Cites the Psalm verse: let those who fear You turn to me
Asks how we know that David's leprosy lasted six months
Cites the Kings verse: the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years

107b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Explains the forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem
Cites the Samuel verse that David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron
These six months are not counted, which proves that David was a leper during them
David asks God to forgive him that sin, and God says it is forgiven
Cites the Psalm verse: show me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see and be ashamed
God says, by your life, I will not tell you, but I will tell you by the life of Solomon your son
When Solomon built the Temple, he sought to bring the ark into the Holy of Holies, and the gates stuck together
Solomon recited twenty-four praises and was not answered
Cites the Psalm verse: lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, ancient doors
Cites the Psalm verse: who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord, mighty in battle
Cites the Psalm verse again: lift up your heads, O gates, and the King of glory shall come in
He was not answered until he said the verse
Cites the Chronicles verse: O Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed, remember the mercies of David Your servant
At that moment the faces of David's enemies turned like the bottom of a pot, all Israel knew God had forgiven him that sin
Asks where Gehazi went, as the verse says Elisha went from Damascus, and where did he go
Rabbi Yochanan says Elisha went to bring Gehazi to repentance but he did not return, since one who sins and causes others to sin cannot repent
Asks what Elisha did
Some say he hung a lodestone for Jeroboam's sin, standing it between heaven and earth
Others say he engraved a name on its mouth so it proclaims: I am the Lord, you shall have no other gods
The other rabbis say he pushed it away from before him
Cites the Kings verse where the sons of the prophets said to Elisha that the place where they dwell is too narrow for them
It follows that until now the place had not been too narrow
The rabbis taught: the left should always repel, and the right should draw near, not like Elisha
Elisha pushed Gehazi with both hands, unlike Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya, who pushed Yeshu with both hands
Cites the Kings verse where Naaman urged Gehazi to take two talents of silver
Cites the Kings verse: Elisha asked Gehazi where he had come from, and Gehazi said your servant went neither here nor there
Cites Gehazi's words in the Kings verse about taking silver, clothes, olives, vineyards and servants
Asks who would take all this silver and clothes, and answers that he is the one who took it
Rabbi Yitzchak says at that time Elisha was sitting and expounding the eight creeping things
Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a leper, and a young Israelite girl taken captive told his wife to go to Elisha
The girl said: if you go to Elisha, he will heal you when he comes
Elisha told him to go and immerse in the Jordan, and he said: are you mocking me?
Those with him said: what do you gain by it, go and try
He went, immersed in the Jordan, and was healed; he brought all the gifts, but Elisha refused to accept them from him, and Gehazi left before him
Gehazi went and took what he took and hid it, and when he came, Elisha saw the leprosy resting on his head
Elisha said: wicked one, now is the time to take a reward of eight creeping things, and Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and your seed forever
Cites the Kings verse that there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate
Rabbi Yochanan says the four were Gehazi and his three sons
Editorial insertion from the deficiencies of the Shas, identifying Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya
Asks what that is
It is as when King Yannai killed the sages
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya and Yeshu fled to Alexandria of Egypt, and when peace came, Shimon ben Shetach sent him a letter from Jerusalem
He came and happened upon an inn where they gave him great honor; he said: how fine is this inn; the owner's eyes were bleary, and he said: wicked one, you are preoccupied with this
He brought out four hundred pilpulim and placed them before him, and one day he was reading the Shema
Yeshu came before him, intending to receive a greeting; he showed him by hand, and he thought he was being pushed away, so he pushed him
He went, lifted a brick and bowed to it, and he said: return
Rabbi Yehoshua says: I have received from you that whoever sins and causes many to sin, they do not allow him to repent
Mar says Yeshu practiced sorcery, incited and led Israel astray
A baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says the left should repel while the right draws near, applied to a child and a woman
A baraita says Elisha suffered three afflictions: a bear sent by him attacked children, he pushed Gehazi with both hands, and one who died from him
Cites the Kings verse that Elisha was sick with the sickness of which he died
Until Abraham there was no old age; whatever Abraham saw he said was Isaac, and Abraham prayed that old age would come to him
Cites the Genesis verse that Abraham was old and advanced in days, and until Jacob there was no weakness
Jacob prayed and weakness came upon him
Cites the Genesis verse: your father is sick, and Joseph came to him
Until Elisha no person became weak who did not recover, and Elisha came and prayed and he recovered
Cites the Kings verse: Elisha was sick with the sickness of which he died
Mishnah: the generation of the flood has no share in the World-to-Come and does not stand in judgment
Cites the Genesis verse: My spirit shall not abide in man forever
Nor the generation of the dispersion has a share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Genesis verse: the Lord scattered them from there over the face of all the earth
Explains that scattering in this world and in the World-to-Come, as the verses about scattering are read
The people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Genesis verse that the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly, in this world and in the World-to-Come
But they do stand in judgment; Rabbi Nechemiah says neither of them stands in judgment
Cites the Psalm verse: therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment

108a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Cites the Psalm verse: therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous
Identifies the wicked and sinners of that verse: the generation of the flood and the people of Sodom, who stand in the congregation of the wicked
The spies who spread a bad report about the land have no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Numbers verse that the men who spread the bad report died by plague before God, both in this world and the World-to-Come
The generation of the desert has no share in the World-to-Come
Nor do they stand in judgment
Cites the Numbers verse that in this desert they shall be consumed and there they shall die
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva
Rabbi Eliezer says that about them the verse speaks
Cites the Psalm verse: gather to Me My pious ones who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice, and the congregation of Korah
The congregation of Korah will not rise in the future
Cites the Numbers verse that the earth covered them, and they perished from among the congregation, for the World-to-Come
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Eliezer says that about them the verse speaks
Cites the Samuel verse: the Lord kills and makes alive, brings down to the grave and raises up
A baraita teaches that the generation of the flood has no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Genesis verse that God wiped out every living thing on the face of the ground, and they were wiped from the earth for the World-to-Come
Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beterah say that they neither live nor are judged
Cites the Genesis verse that My spirit shall not abide in man forever, with the gloss that their soul does not return to its place
Rabbi Menachem bar Yosef says that even when God restores souls to dead bodies, their soul is hard for them in Gehenna
Cites the Isaiah verse: you conceive chaff and bring forth stubble, and your breath is a fire that will devour you
A baraita teaches that the generation of the flood was not arrogant except because of the good God had given them
Asks what is written about them
Cites the Job verse: their houses are safe from fear, and God's rod is not upon them
Cites the Job verse: their ox mates without fail, their cow calves and does not miscarry
Cites the Job verse: they send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance, they sing to the timbrel and harp
Cites the Job verse: they spend their days in prosperity, and in a moment go down to Sheol; they say to God, depart from us, we do not desire knowledge of Your ways
They said: do we need Him? We need only a drop of rain, since we have rivers and springs
God said: with the good I gave them they anger Me, so with it I will judge them
Cites the Genesis verse: and I, behold, I will bring the flood of waters
Rabbi Yossi says the generation of the flood was arrogant only because of the eye's spring, which resembles water
Cites the Genesis verse that they took wives from all whom they chose
Therefore God judged them with water, which resembles the eye's spring
Cites the Genesis verse that all the fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of heaven opened
Rabbi Yochanan says the generation of the flood sinned with abundance and was judged with abundance
Cites the Genesis verses about God seeing the great wickedness of man, and all the fountains of the great deep
Rabbi Yochanan says three were left of them: the hollow of Gadar, the hot springs of Tiberias, and the great springs of Beirum
Cites the Genesis verse about the hot springs
Cites the Genesis verse: all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth
Rabbi Yochanan teaches that they mated animals with beasts, beasts with animals, and all with man, and man with all
Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says all of them repented except Methuselah
Cites the Genesis verse: God said to Noah that the end of all flesh had come before Me
Rabbi Yochanan says see how great is the power of robbery, since the generation of the flood transgressed everything, yet their sentence was not sealed until they stretched out their hands to robbery
Cites the Genesis verse that the earth was full of violence because of them, and I will destroy them with the earth
Cites the Ezekiel verse: violence rose up into a rod of wickedness, none of them remains, none of their multitude
Rabbi Elazar teaches that the verse shows one who stood like a staff before God and said: none of them, none of their multitude remains
Even on Noah a sentence was sealed, as it is stated that Noah did not rest with them
A teaching of the school of Rabbi Yishmael: even on Noah the sentence was not sealed, because he found favor in God's eyes
Cites the Genesis verses: I regret that I made them, and Noah found favor in God's eyes; God regretted that He made man on the earth
When Rav Dimi came, he said God said: I did well to create graves for them in the earth
Asks what this implies, since the word vayinnachem is written here
Compares the Genesis verse where it is written vayinnachem here, with the verse there where God comforted them and spoke to their hearts
Others say: I did not do well to create graves for them in the earth
Cites the Exodus verse that God regretted the evil He had spoken of doing to His people, and the Genesis verse about Noah
Cites the Genesis verse: these are the generations of Noah, Noah was a righteous man, perfect in his generations
Rabbi Yochanan says in his generations, not in other generations; Resh Lakish says in his generations, all the more so in other generations
Rabbi Chanina gives Rabbi Yochanan's parable: a wine cask placed in a vinegar cellar, whose aroma does not spread when not in its place
Resh Lakish's parable: a bottle of perfume placed in a place of filth, whose aroma spreads, and all the more so in a place of perfume
Cites the Genesis verse that God wiped out every living thing on the face of the earth
Asks: if man sinned, what did the beast sin
A teaching in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha: a parable of a man who prepared a wedding and a feast for his son, and then his son died
He tore down the wedding canopy and said: I did it only for my son, now that he died, what is the wedding to me
So too God said: did I create beast and animal except for man, and now that man sins, what are beast and animal to Me
Cites the Genesis verse that everything in whose nostrils was the breath of life died, but not the fish of the sea
Rabbi Yossi of Kesari expounded: what is written
Cites the Job verse: he is light upon the face of the waters, their portion is cursed in the land
This teaches that Noah the righteous rebuked them and said: repent, and if not, God will bring the flood upon you, and your carcasses will float like straw
Cites the Job verse: he is light upon the face of the waters
Moreover, they take from them a curse for all who come into the world
Cites the Job verse: their portion is cursed in the land
Cites the Job verse: he does not turn the way of the vineyards
This teaches that they used to turn aside the way of the vineyards
He said to them: who is stopping me? He said to them: I have one parting to take from you

108b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: So they would not turn aside the way of the vineyards
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Job verse: a torch of scorn for the thoughts of the secure, ready for the time of the foot's slipping
Explains the verse: Noah the righteous rebuked the people with words as sharp as torches, and they mocked him
They said to him: old man, why this ark?
Noah said: God is bringing the flood upon you
They said: a flood of what? If of fire, we have another matter, and we will go up there
If of water, we have iron plates with which we cover the earth; if from the earth, we have nothing else
If it comes from the heavens, we have a matter: the heel, Akkov is its name, also called Ekesh
Noah said: He will bring them to the heels of your feet
Cites the Job verse about the time of the foot's slipping
A baraita: the waters of the flood were hard, like the discharge of seed
Cites the Job verse about the time of the foot's slipping
Rav Chisda says they were corrupted by heat in transgression and judged by heat
Cites the Genesis verse that the waters subsided, and the Esther verse where the king's wrath subsided
Cites the Genesis verse: after seven days the flood waters were upon the earth
Asks what the nature of those seven days was
Rav says they were the days of mourning for Methuselah, to teach that the eulogies of the righteous delay calamity
Another explanation: God changed the order of creation for those seven days, so the sun rose in the west and set in the east, and then a long time, then a short time
Another explanation: the seven days gave them a taste of the World-to-Come, so they would know what good they had been denied
So they would know what goodness they had been denied
Cites the Genesis verse: take seven pairs of every clean animal
Seven of each, man and his wife, the pairs of marital relations
Asks whether an animal has marital relations
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, citing Rabbi Yonatan, says these are the animals in which no transgression was committed
How did he know? Rav Chisda says he passed them before the ark, and the ark took in those in which no transgression was committed, while it did not take in those in which transgression was committed
Rabbi Abbahu says these are from those that come by themselves
Cites the Genesis verse: make yourself an ark of gopher wood
Asks what gopher wood is
Rav Adda says in the school of Rabbi Shila it is called mablige, and others call it gulmish
Cites the Genesis verse: make a window for the ark
Rabbi Yochanan says God told Noah to set into the ark good stones and pearls, so that they would shine for you like noon
Cites the Genesis verse: and to a cubit you shall finish it from above
With that it stands
Cites the Genesis verse: with lower, second and third decks you shall make it
A tanna teaches: the lower deck for dung, the middle for animals, the upper for man
Cites the Genesis verse: he sent out the raven
Resh Lakish says the raven gave Noah a victorious reply

The raven said to Noah: your Master hates me, and you hate me; your Master hates me, since you took seven of the clean and two of the unclean, and you hate me because you leave a species of seven and send out of a species of two
If I meet the sun's officer or the cold officer, the world will not be missing one creature; or perhaps you need my mate for yourself
Noah, wicked one, said: what is in excess is forbidden to me, and the forbidden is forbidden to me, and all the more so
Asks how we know that they were forbidden
Cites the Genesis verses: you and your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives enter the ark, and go out from the ark, you and your wife
From here Rabbi Yochanan says they were forbidden marital relations in the bed
A baraita teaches: three served in the ark, and all were punished: the dog was tied, the raven was rebuked, and Ham was stricken in his skin
Cites the Genesis verse: he sent out the dove from him to see whether the waters had subsided
Rabbi Yirmeya says from here that the dwelling of clean birds is with the righteous
Cites the Genesis verse: and behold, an olive leaf torn off in her mouth
Rabbi Elazar says the dove said before God: let my food be bitter as an olive, given into Your hand, and not sweet as honey given into flesh and blood's hand
Asks what it implies that the word for torn-off food is used for sustenance
Cites the Proverbs verse: feed me with the bread of my portion
Cites the Genesis verse: they went out of the ark according to their families
Rabbi Yochanan says to their families, and not they themselves, meaning the families were not the ones who went out
Rav Chana bar Bizna reports that Eliezer was challenged by Shem about the wording of the verse that they went out of the ark by families
Cites the Genesis verse: they went out of the ark according to their families
Asks: where were you?

Eliezer said: it was a great pain for us in the ark; we had a creature whose habit was to feed in the day, and we fed it at night; a lion did not know what it ate; one day it sat and split a pomegranate, a worm fell from it, and the lion at
From then on the animal was given a lump of food when it gnawed; Rav says it ate no less than six and no more than twelve measures
Abba found the animal feeding at the side of the ark, and the story continues about its food
He asked: did you not want food?
He replied: I saw you were busy, so I did not want to trouble you
May it be His will that you will not die
Cites the Job verse: I shall die in my nest, and multiply my days like the sand
Rav Chana bar Luai says
Shem said to Eliezer: when the kings of the east and west came upon you, how did you act
Eliezer said: God brought Abraham and seated him at His right, and they threw dust, swords became straw and bows became stubble
Cites the Psalm verse: the Lord says to my lord, sit at My right hand until I make your enemies your footstool
Cites the Isaiah verse: who has raised up one from the east, calls him to His foot, gives nations before him, and makes him rule kings
Cites the Isaiah verse: his sword makes them like dust, and his bow like driven stubble
Nachum Ish Gam Zu used to say: this too is for the good, whenever something happened to him
One day Israel wanted to send a gift to the emperor, and they said

109a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Asks who was sent along with Nachum
Nachum Ish Gam Zu, who was accustomed to miracles, was the one sent
When he came to an inn and wanted to lodge there, they asked what he carried; he said he was carrying a tax for the emperor
At night they rose, opened his sack, took everything he had, and filled it with dust
He said the Judeans were mocking him, so they took him out to kill him
He said: this too is for the good
Elijah came and appeared to them as one of them, and said to them
Perhaps this dust is from the dust of our father Abraham
Abraham had thrown dust, and swords became plowshares; they tested the city and found it could not be conquered until they threw that dust on it
They brought him to the treasury, he filled his sack with gold, and on his return the innkeepers asked about it; he killed the innkeepers in turn
Mishnah: the generation of the dispersion has no share in the World-to-Come
Asks what they did
The school of Rabbi Shila says they built a tower to ascend to the sky and strike it with axes so its waters would flow out
In the West they say: let us build one on a mountain
Rav Yirmeya bar Elazar says they split into three factions: one would settle there, one would worship idols, and one would wage war, which is why God scattered them
Cites the Genesis verse that God confused the language of all the earth there
A baraita: Rabbi Natan says all of them intended the name of idol worship
Cites the Genesis verse: let us make a name for ourselves, and the Exodus verse: you shall not mention the names of other gods, so here too it means idol worship
Rabbi Yochanan says one third of the tower burned, one third was swallowed, and one third remains
Rav says the tower was found in the air
Rav Yosef says Babel and Borsif are a bad sign for Torah
Asks what Borsif is
Rabbi Asi says it is a pit that is deep
Mishnah: the people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come
A baraita: the people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Genesis verse that the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly, in this world and in the World-to-Come
Rav Yehuda says they were wicked in their bodies and sinners in their property
Cites the Genesis verse: how then could I do this great evil and sin against God
They were sinners in their property
Cites the Deuteronomy verse: lest there be a sin in you against the Lord, this is the blessing of the Name very much
The sinners intend to sin, as in the baraita
A baraita: they were wicked in their property and sinners in their bodies
Cites the Deuteronomy verse: your eye be evil toward your needy brother
And sinners in their bodies
Cites the Genesis verse: I would sin against God
Explains: this is the blessing of the Name very much, and this is bloodshed
Cites the Kings verse: Manasseh shed much innocent blood in Jerusalem
A baraita: the men of Sodom became arrogant only because of the good God gave them
Asks what is written about them
Cites the Job verses about bread coming out of the earth and gold dust in it, and the path no bird of prey knows
They said: since bread and gold dust come out of the land, why should travelers come to us except to diminish us; come, let us forget the laws of the road from our land
Cites the Job verse: the stream breaks out away from the inhabitant, forgotten by the foot
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Psalm verse: how long will you attack a man, all of you, like a leaning wall
Explains: they would fix their eyes on wealthy people, seat them next to a leaning wall, push them onto it, and take their property
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Job verse: thieves break into houses by night, they shut themselves in by day and do not know the light
Explains: they would fix their eyes on wealthy people, deposit perfume with them, and place it in their treasure house, then come at evening to smell it like a dog
They come and smell it like a dog
Cites the Psalm verse: they return at evening, howl like a dog, and go around the city
They come, dig through there, and take the property
Cites the Job verse: they go naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold
Cites the Job verses about the donkeys of the orphans and the ox of the widow, and the one who is buried with honor and watches the heap
Rabbi Yossi expounded in Tzippori: three hundred burglars came one night to dig through
They told him he had shown the way to thieves; he said he did not know thieves would come; when Rabbi Yossi died, the gutters of Tzippori flowed with blood
They say he had an ox grazing, and an orphan son of a widow was given oxen to graze; he took and killed them, and said to them

109b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: In Sodom, one who has an ox takes one hide from one without an ox, and two hides from one who has two
They asked him what this is
He said: the end of the law is like its beginning
Just as the one who has an ox grazes it one day, and the one without oxen grazes two days, so at the end of the law, one who has one ox takes one from one without, and one without takes two
One who crosses at the ferry pays one zuz, while one who does not cross pays two
Each one took a share of the ox, and each one who had cast off the hides took a share
There were four judges in Sodom, who were false, falsified judgments and struck
They struck a woman who had hurt her fellow and gave her to them, to be pierced
They said: I will cut off the donkey's ear of the other
They said: give it to him until it burns and strikes his fellow
They told him the fee: the one who crosses by blood pays four zuz, the one who crosses in water pays eight
Once a launderer came there, and they said to him: pay four zuz; he said: I crossed in water; they said: then pay eight zuz for having crossed in water
He came before the judge, who said: pay him the fee, since you took the blood, and eight zuz for having crossed in water
Eliezer, Abraham's servant, happened to be there and ransomed him; he took a stone and ransomed himself, and said to the judge: what is this
The judge replied: the fee that comes out of you, give it to him, and my zuz are as they stand; the blankets they used to protect the guests
When the guests stretched him long, they cut him short, like a dwarf stretching
Eliezer, Abraham's servant, came, and they said to him: get up and water the blankets; he said to them: since the day my mother died I vowed not to water them
When a poor man came to them, each gave him a dinar
Written on it is his name, and they did not give him bread; when he died, each came and took his own
So they stipulated among themselves: whoever invites a man to a wedding should send him a garment
Whoever invites a man to a wedding should send him a garment
Eliezer came to that wedding, and they did not give him bread when he wanted to eat
He came and sat at the end of them all, and they said to him
Who invited you here
He said to one sitting there: you invited them
He said: perhaps they will hear about me that I invited him, and sent him the clothes of this man
He took the cloak of the one sitting next to him, ran outside, did so to all of them, until they all went out, and then he himself ate the feast
A girl brought bread to the poor in a pitcher; the matter was revealed when they poured honey over it, and they set it on the wall, and bees came and ate it
Cites the Genesis verse: the outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great
Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, says this is about the matter of their outcry
The spies have no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Numbers verse that the men who spread the bad report died by plague
The congregation of Korah has no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Numbers verse: the earth covered them, and they perished from among the congregation
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Eliezer says that about them the verse speaks
Cites the Samuel verse: the Lord kills and makes alive, brings down to the grave and raises up
A baraita: the congregation of Korah has no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Numbers verse that the earth covered them, and they perished from among the congregation for the World-to-Come
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says they are like a lost article that is sought
They are like a lost sheep
Cites the Psalm verse: I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments

Resh Lakish says Korah made a bad purchase for himself: he became bald in Israel, son of Yitzhar who heated the world like noon, son of Kohath who dulled his teeth, son of Levi who became a Levite in Gehenna
Let us also consider Jacob's son who pulled himself toward Gehenna
Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak says Jacob asked for mercy for himself
Cites the Genesis verse: into their council let my soul not come, for in their assembly let my glory not be united, the spies and the congregation of Korah

This is the congregation of Korah, Dathan who transgressed God's law, Abiram who would not repent, and On ben Peleth who sat in mourning and was saved by his wife, a son of Reuben who saw and understood
Rav says On ben Peleth
His wife saved him: she said to him, what do you gain from it; if the master is great, you are the disciple, and if the master is great, you are the disciple
He said: what shall I do, I was in the counsel and swore with them
She said: I know that the whole congregation is holy, as it is written
Cites the Numbers verse: for all the congregation are holy
She said: return, I will save you; she gave him wine, made him drunk, brought him inside, and sat him at the door

110a.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: Korah's wife hid things; when he came back she saw, and in the meantime they were swallowed
Korah's wife said to him: see what Moses does; he was king and made his brother the high priest, and his sons the deputies of the priesthood
If heave-offering comes, it is for the priest, and if tithes, you took them; give one ox to the priest
Further, he cut his cloak for you, and rubbed the eyes of the people; behold, he too does this
She said: since all the greatness is his, he too
Cites the Judges verse: let me die with the Philistines
Further, he told you to make blue wool; if blue is esteemed, take out blue garments and cover all of them
Cites the Proverbs verse: the wise women build their house, but the foolish tears it down, which refers to the wives of On ben Peleth and Korah
Cites the Numbers verse about two hundred fifty men of Israel called to the assembly, men of renown
Moses fell on his face; what report did he hear
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, citing Rabbi Yonatan, says they suspected Moses of adultery with a married woman
Cites the Psalm verse that they were jealous of Moses in the camp
Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak teaches that each one was jealous of Moses regarding his wife
Cites the Exodus verse that Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, and the Numbers verse about Dathan and Abiram
Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram
Resh Lakish says from here one should not hold on to dispute; as Rav said, whoever holds on to dispute transgresses a prohibition
Cites the Numbers verse: that he not be like Korah and his congregation
Rav Ashi says one deserves to be stricken with leprosy, as is written here about Moses
Cites the Exodus verse: put your hand into your bosom, and it became leprous
Rabbi Yosei says whoever disputes the kingship of the house of David deserves to be bitten by a snake
Cites the Kings verse about Adonijah sacrificing sheep and oxen and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth
Cites the Deuteronomy verse about the venom of creeping things of the dust
Rav Chisda says whoever disputes his teacher is as one who disputes the Divine Presence
Cites the Numbers verse: when they contended against the Lord
Rabbi Chama bar Rabbi Chanina says whoever creates strife with his teacher is as one who creates strife with the Divine Presence
Cites the Numbers verse: these are the waters of Meribah, where the children of Israel strove with the Lord
Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa says whoever complains about his teacher is as if he complains about the Divine Presence
Cites the Exodus verse: your complaints are not against us, but against the Lord
Rabbi Abbahu says whoever murmurs against his teacher is as if he murmurs against the Divine Presence
Cites the Numbers verse: the people spoke against God and against Moses
Cites the Ecclesiastes verse: riches kept by their owner to their harm
Resh Lakish says this is the wealth of Korah
Cites the Deuteronomy verse: and all the substance which was under their feet
Rabbi Elazar says this is a person's property that he stands on his own feet
Rabbi Levi says Korah's treasure house had keys carried by three hundred white mules, and all its keys were like the peels of a leek
Rabbi Chama bar Rabbi Chanina says Joseph hid three treasures in Egypt: one was revealed to Korah, one was revealed to Antoninus son of Asverus, and one is hidden for the righteous in the future
Rabbi Yochanan says Korah was neither of those swallowed nor of those burned, but of those swallowed
Cites the Numbers verse about all the men who belonged to Korah, and not Korah, nor of those burned
Cites the Numbers verse about the fire consuming the two hundred fifty men, and not Korah
A baraita teaches that Korah was of the burned and of the swallowed, as the Numbers verse says it swallowed them
Cites the Numbers verse: and it swallowed them
Korah was of the burned, as the verse says
Cites the Numbers verse: a fire came forth from before the Lord and consumed the two hundred fifty men
The two hundred fifty men and Korah were with them
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Habakkuk verse: the sun and moon stood still in their habitation, at the light of Your arrows
This teaches that the sun and moon went up to Zevulun, and they said before God, Master of the World
If You do justice for the son of Amram we will go out, and if not we will not go out
Until He shot arrows into them; He said: for My honor I did not destroy them through the honor of flesh and blood, and now they will not come out until they strike them
Rava expounds, asking what is written
Cites the Numbers verse: if the Lord creates a new thing and the earth opens its mouth
Moses said before God: if Gehenna is created, good; if not, let God create it for what purpose
Shall we say it is created as a real creation? But it is written there is nothing new under the sun
Cites the Ecclesiastes verse that there is nothing new under the sun, and explains that it was created to open a mouth
Cites the Numbers verse that the children of Korah did not die
A tanna taught in the name of our teacher: a place was fortified for them in Gehenna, and they sat upon it and recited a song
Rabba bar bar Chana related: once, as I was walking on the road, a dyer said to me: come and I will show you the place where Korah was swallowed, and I saw two openings from which smoke rose

He took a bundle of wool, dipped it in water, and placed it on the tip of his spear, and it was burned there; he said: do you hear what they were saying, that Moses and his Torah are true, and they are false

110b.source: Machine-assisted draft of the Vilna text; awaiting editorial review

ranges.en: For thirty days Gehenna returns them like meat in a pot, and they say: Moses and his Torah are true, and they are false
Mishnah: the generation of the desert has no share in the World-to-Come
A baraita teaches the same: the generation of the desert has no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Numbers verse: in this desert they shall be consumed, and there they shall die
Cites the Psalm verse: as I swore in My anger that they shall not enter My rest
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Eliezer says they come to the World-to-Come
Cites the Psalm verse: gather to Me My pious ones who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice
Rather, how does God fulfill what He swore in His anger, since He reversed it
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says this verse was not said except in reference to the generations to come
Explains that the pious ones are the righteous of every generation, such as Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah, who gave themselves into the furnace
Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues who gave themselves to slaughter for the words of Torah
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says they come to the World-to-Come
Cites the Isaiah verse: the ransomed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing
Rabba bar bar Chana said: Rabbi Yochanan said Rabbi Akiva left aside his piety
Cites the Jeremiah verse: go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, I remember the kindness of your youth; if others come on their merit, all the more so these themselves
Mishnah: the ten tribes will not return, as stated in Deuteronomy
Cites the Deuteronomy verse: He cast them into another land as this day; as the day goes and does not return, so they go and do not return
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Eliezer says the day is as this day
As one day darkens and then lightens, so the ten tribes, whose darkness will be lit for them in the future
A baraita teaches that the ten tribes have no share in the World-to-Come
Cites the Deuteronomy verse: God uprooted them from their land in anger and fury, and cast them into another land, for the World-to-Come
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva; Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of Kfar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon
